chunks: Al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If two or three men have intercourse with a bondwoman in one period of purity, then she gives birth, and all of them claim the child, the ruler draws lots between them. Whoever is selected by the lot, the child is his, and he returns the value of the child to the owner of the bondwoman.

He said: If a man buys a bondwoman, then another man comes and rightfully establishes his claim to her, and she has given birth from the buyer, the bondwoman is returned to him, and her child belongs to the buyer for its value.

key_terms.أَقْرَعَ: he drew lots to determine the ruling claimant
key_terms.اسْتَحَقَّهَا: he rightfully established his claim to her
key_terms.الْوَالِي: the governing authority or ruler who administers the lot
key_terms.الْوَلَدُ: the child whose attribution is being determined
key_terms.طُهْرٍ: a period of purity in which the intercourse occurred
key_terms.قِيمَةَ: the monetary value to be paid as compensation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if multiple men claim a child born from a bondwoman, or if a sold bondwoman is later reclaimed by her rightful owner?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings for disputed paternity and ownership involving a bondwoman and her child. It establishes recourse to drawing lots by the wali in a case of competing claims, and it also rules on compensation when ownership of the bondwoman is restored to her rightful owner while the child is assigned to the buyer with payment of value.
